copy.en:
How does activated charcoal help with poisoning?

Its tiny holes give huge surface area to soak up stomach poison before absorption. It's not a home remedy; only a doctor should give it, and it doesn't work on every poison.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakatulong ang activated charcoal sa lason?

Dahil sa maraming butas, malaki ang surface area kaya nasisipsip ang lason sa tiyan bago masipsip ng katawan. Hindi gamot sa bahay; doktor lang ang magbibigay, hindi gumagana sa lahat ng lason.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtabang sa activated charcoal sa hilo?

Sa daghang lungag, dako ang surface area busa masuyop ang hilo sa tiyan sa dili pa masuyop sa lawas. Dili tambal sa balay; doktor ra ang mohatag, dili molihok sa tanang hilo.

Is an active fault the same as a plate edge?

Not exactly! An active fault is just a moving crack in the ground, while a plate boundary is the giant edge of huge earth slabs — a fault can even sit inside a plate.

Pareho ba ang active fault at gilid ng tectonic plate?

Hindi eksakto! Ang active fault ay isang bitak lang sa lupa na gumagalaw, habang ang tectonic plate boundary ay ang malaking dulo ng higanteng tipak ng lupa — puwede pa itong makita sa loob ng isang plate.
copy.bis:
Pareho ba ang active fault ug ngilit sa tectonic plate?

Dili eksaktong parehas! Ang active fault usa lang ka liki sa yuta nga nagalihok; ang plate boundary mao ang dako nga ngilit tali sa higante nga mga tipak sa yuta.

Dili! Dugay ang pag-ayo sa uma ug paglimpyo sa abo. Mao nga ang 'after' usa ka taas nga yugto, dili lang usa ka hapon!

Mahitabo kini tungod kay ang presyon sa hangin sa gawas mausab nga mas paspas kay sa sulod sa dalunggan!

copy.bis:

Kung mosupsop ka sa straw, gikuha nimo ang hangin sa sulod niini, busa ang presyon sa hangin moduot sa ilimnon pataas ngadto sa imong baba!

Pinakataas ang air pressure duol sa yuta! Samtang mosaka ka og mas taas, sama sa bukid, mohuyang kini.

copy.bis:
Unsa ang duha ka bahin sa split-type nga aircon?

Adunay duha ka bahin kini: ang sulod nga magpabugnaw, ug ang gawas nga mopagawas sa kainit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it has no thermostat to measure the room's heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions measuring room heat with a thermostat but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature, so it does not directly support G7-F-8.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Only the aircon uses a thermostat to measure heat!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a household appliance and heat measurement, but it does not identify sources and uses of heat energy in the way G4-F-10 requires.

copy.en:
Why doesn't an ordinary electric fan stop by itself when the room is cool?

Because it has no thermostat to measure the room's heat! It just blows at your chosen speed, so you must switch it off by hand. Only the aircon uses a thermostat to measure heat!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi kusang humihinto ang ordinaryong electric fan kapag malamig na ang kwarto?

Dahil wala itong thermostat para sukatin ang init ng kwarto! Umiihip lang ito sa speed na pinili mo, kaya kailangan mong patayin nang mano-mano. Ang aircon lang ang may thermostat para sukatin ang init!
copy.bis:
Ngano dili kusang mohunong ang electric fan kon bugnaw na?

Walay thermostat kini aron sukdon ang init! Mohuyop lang sa speed nga imong gipili, mao nga kinahanglan nimo palungon sa kamot. Ang aircon ra ang naay thermostat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Setting the aircon to 16°C doesn't cool the room faster!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses thermostat temperature settings and cooling rate, but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It does not directly support the competency's concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It just runs longer before stopping, which uses more electricity!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that power is the rate of doing work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions electricity usage but does not define power as the rate of doing work. It does not directly teach the competency's core concept.

copy.en: Setting the aircon to 16°C doesn't cool the room faster! It blows cold at the same rate. It just runs longer before stopping, which uses more electricity!
copy.tl: Ang pag-set ng aircon sa 16°C ay hindi nakakapagpalamig ng mas mabilis! Pareho lang ang bilis. Mas matagal lang itong gagana bago huminto, kaya mas malakas ang kuryente!
copy.bis: Ang pag-set sa aircon sa 16°C dili makapabugnaw og mas paspas! Pareho ra ang paspas. Mas dugay lang siya modagan bago mohunong, mao nga mas dako ang kuryente!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After the compressor turns off, leftover cold air keeps blowing!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a set temperature (24°C) and cold air but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It describes a thermostat overshoot phenomenon, not the conceptual distinction between heat and temperature.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: leftover cold air keeps blowing
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to cold air blowing, which could involve convection, but it does not identify or classify examples of conduction, convection, or radiation as advantageous or disadvantageous. The focus is on thermostat overshoot, not heat transfer mechanisms.

copy.en: Wondering why your room feels colder than the set 24°C? After the compressor turns off, leftover cold air keeps blowing! This slight overshoot is temporary and quickly settles back to your target warmth.
copy.tl: Bakit minsan mas malamig pa sa set 24°C ang kwarto? Kahit pumatay na ang compressor, patuloy pa ring umiihip ang natitirang malamig na hangin! Pansamantala lang ang overshoot na ito at babalik sa tamang init.
copy.bis: Ngano usahay mas bugnaw pa sa set 24°C ang kwarto? Bisan napalong na ang compressor, padayon pa gihapong mobuga ang nahabilin nga bugnaw nga hangin! Temporaryo ra ang overshoot ug mobalik sa husto nga init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lift pushes it up, weight pulls it down, thrust from the engines pushes it forward, and drag from the air holds it back.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card names four forces on an airplane but does not discuss whether they are balanced or unbalanced, nor does it connect them to the competency's examples of balanced/unbalanced force situations. It provides vocabulary about forces but no direct instruction on the balanced/unbalanced concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lift pushes it up, weight pulls it down, thrust from the engines pushes it forward, and drag from the air holds it back.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes forces acting on an airplane, which implies forces act between objects, but it does not address measurement of forces or the general principle that forces act between objects. It is only tangentially related to the competency's focus on force measurement.

copy.en:
What four forces keep an airplane flying?

Lift pushes it up, weight pulls it down, thrust from the engines pushes it forward, and drag from the air holds it back.
copy.tl:
Anong apat na puwersa ang nagpapalipad sa eroplano?

Ang lift ay nagtutulak pataas, ang bigat ay humihila pababa, ang thrust mula sa makina ay nagtutulak pasulong, at ang drag mula sa hangin ay pumipigil dito.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang upat ka puwersa nga nagpalupad sa eroplano?

Ang lift motulod pataas, ang gibug-aton mobira paubos, ang thrust gikan sa makina motulod pasulong, ug ang drag gikan sa hangin mopugong niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Akapulko leaves are approved by the DOH to treat ringworm and other skin fungus
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a medicinal use of a plant for humans, but does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It is only tangentially related to living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: just mash them into a paste and apply
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions mashing leaves into a paste, which is a change in a solid material, but it does not describe how such changes make materials useful in the sense of shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, or cutting. The focus is on medicinal application, not on material properties or usefulness.

copy.en: Akapulko leaves are approved by the DOH to treat ringworm and other skin fungus — just mash them into a paste and apply.
copy.tl: Ang dahon ng akapulko ay DOH-approved para gamutin ang buni at iba pang fungal na sakit sa balat — dinudurog lang ito bilang paste at inilalapat sa apektadong bahagi.
copy.bis: Ang dahon sa akapulko DOH-approved para tambalan ang buni ug uban pang fungal nga sakit sa balat — dugmokon lang isip paste ug ibutang sa apektadong bahin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bright white ice reflects sunlight back to space! When it melts, it exposes darker water or land that absorbs more heat, speeding up the warming even more.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the ice-albedo feedback mechanism, which is a consequence/amplifier of global warming, but it does not present evidence of global warming or climate change (e.g., temperature records, sea-level rise, glacial retreat data). It explains a process rather than identifying evidence, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bright white ice reflects sunlight back to space! When it melts, it exposes darker water or land that absorbs more heat, speeding up the warming even more.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves reflection and absorption of heat (radiation), but it does not identify advantageous or disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, or radiation in everyday contexts. It only touches on radiative reflection/absorption without framing it as an example of heat transfer for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bright white ice reflects sunlight back to space! When it melts, it exposes darker water or land that absorbs more heat, speeding up the warming even more.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how solar energy interacts with Earth's surface (reflection and absorption), but it does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. The focus is on surface albedo and feedback, not atmospheric interaction, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Bright white ice reflects sunlight back to space! When it melts, it exposes darker water or land that absorbs more heat, speeding up the warming even more.
copy.tl: Ang maputing yelo ay nagsasalamin ng sinag ng araw pabalik sa kalawakan! Kapag natunaw ito, nalalantad ang madilim na tubig o lupa na sumisipsip ng mas maraming init, na nagpapabilis sa pag-init.
copy.bis: Ang puti nga yelo nagasalming sa kahayag sa adlaw balik sa kawanangan! Kung matunaw kini, mabutyag ang mas itom nga tubig o yuta nga mosuyop og dugang kainit, nga magpadali pa sa pag-init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PHIVOLCS uses alert levels from 0 to 5 to show how close a volcano is to erupting!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that PHIVOLCS alert levels exist and indicate eruption proximity. It does not explain what each alert level means, nor does it demonstrate what to do before, during, or after an eruption, which are the core actions of the competency. This is useful background but not direct instructional support.

copy.en:
How do we know if a volcano is about to erupt?

PHIVOLCS uses alert levels from 0 to 5 to show how close a volcano is to erupting!
copy.tl:
Paano natin malalaman kung malapit nang pumutok ang isang bulkan?

Gumagamit ang PHIVOLCS ng mga antas ng alerto mula 0 hanggang 5 upang ipakita kung gaano kalapit pumutok ang isang bulkan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagkahibalo kung duol na mobuto ang bulkan?

Naggamit ang PHIVOLCS og mga lebel sa alerto gikan sa 0 hangtod 5 aron ipakita kung unsa kaduol mobuto ang usa ka bulkan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PHIVOLCS uses alert levels from 0 to 5 to show exactly how dangerous a volcano is right now!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that PHIVOLCS alert levels exist and indicate danger. It does not interpret the levels or demonstrate what to do before, during, and after an eruption, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en: PHIVOLCS uses alert levels from 0 to 5 to show exactly how dangerous a volcano is right now!
copy.tl: Gumagamit ang PHIVOLCS ng alert level mula 0 hanggang 5 para ipakita kung gaano kapanganib ang isang bulkan ngayon!
copy.bis: Naggamit ang PHIVOLCS og alert level gikan 0 hangtod 5 aron ipakita kon unsa ka delikado ang bulkan karon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coralline algae store calcium carbonate in their cell walls, cementing coral reefs together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions coral reefs and a biotic organism (coralline algae) but does not describe the biotic and abiotic features of coral reefs as required. It provides a single fact about reef cementation, not a description of ecosystem features.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coralline algae store calcium carbonate in their cell walls
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: Coralline algae are not plants and the card does not address specialized plant structures such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Coralline algae store calcium carbonate in their cell walls, cementing coral reefs together and making them stronger!
copy.tl: Nagtatago ng calcium carbonate sa cell wall nito ang coralline algae — tumutulong itong magbigay-tibay sa istruktura ng coral reef!
copy.bis: Nagdeposito og calcium carbonate sa cell wall ang coralline algae — nagpalig-on kini sa istruktura sa coral reef!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An algal bloom is a sudden, rapid increase in plankton that happens when the water has plenty of nutrients and warmth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an algal bloom as a rapid increase in plankton due to nutrients and warmth. While plankton are living (biotic) and nutrients/warmth are non-living (abiotic), the card does not teach the competency's core skill of describing living things as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type as abiotic factors. It only provides a specific example without explicitly framing or explaining the biotic/abiotic factor concepts.

copy.en:
What is an algal bloom?

An algal bloom is a sudden, rapid increase in plankton that happens when the water has plenty of nutrients and warmth.
copy.tl:
Ano ang algal bloom?

Ang algal bloom ay ang biglaan at mabilis na pagdami ng plankton kapag sobra ang sustansya at init sa tubig.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang algal bloom?

Ang algal bloom mao ang kalit ug paspas nga pagdaghan sa plankton kung daghan ang sustansya ug init sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Almost every cell in your body has the exact same genes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses differential gene expression (different sets of genes turned on in different cell types), not the transmission of traits from parents to offspring. It does not explain the role of DNA, genes, or chromosomes in inheritance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Almost every cell in your body has the exact same genes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that body cells (many cells in a multicellular human) share the same genes, but it does not contrast unicellular organisms (like bacteria) with multicellular organisms, nor does it teach the concept of unicellular vs. multicellular organization.

copy.en:
Why do body cells act so differently?

Almost every cell in your body has the exact same genes, but each type turns on a different set — that's why they do different jobs.
copy.tl:
Bakit magkaiba ang trabaho ng mga selula?

Halos lahat ng selula sa katawan mo ay may parehong genes, pero iba-iba ang aktibo sa bawat uri — kaya magkaiba ang kanilang trabaho.
copy.bis:
Nganong lahi ang buhat sa mga selula?

Halos tanang selula sa imong lawas adunay pareho nga mga gene, apan lahi ang aktibo sa matag matang — mao nga lahi ang ilang buhat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All electromagnetic waves, including ultraviolet and infrared, travel at the exact same speed of light in empty space.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a property of EM waves (same speed) but does not describe EMR as energy created by vibrations of charged particles or as transverse waves, which is the core of G9-F-10.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All electromagnetic waves, including ultraviolet and infrared, travel at the exact same speed of light in empty space.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions EM wave types but does not compare relative wavelengths or frequencies, which is the required skill of G9-F-11.

copy.en:
Who wins the ultimate light race in space?

It's a tie! All electromagnetic waves, including ultraviolet and infrared, travel at the exact same speed of light in empty space.
copy.tl:
Sino ang mananalo sa pinakamabilis na karera ng liwanag sa space?

Pantay sila! Lahat ng electromagnetic wave, pati ultraviolet at infrared, ay naglalakbay sa parehong bilis ng liwanag sa kawalan.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang modagan sa pinakaspas nga karera sa kahayag sa space?

Pantay sila! Tanang electromagnetic wave, apil ang ultraviolet ug infrared, nagapanaw sa managsama nga tulin sa kahayag sa wala.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the energy in it first came from sunlight, captured through photosynthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that food energy originates from sunlight via photosynthesis. It does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Almost all food traces back to plants — and the energy in it first came from sunlight
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use examples of food pyramids to describe the transfer of energy between organisms from one trophic level to another
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the ultimate source of food energy (sunlight via plants) but does not mention food pyramids, trophic levels, or energy transfer between organisms. It is unrelated to the specific competency about using food pyramid examples to describe trophic-level energy transfer.

copy.en:
Where does all our food's energy come from?

Almost all food traces back to plants — and the energy in it first came from sunlight, captured through photosynthesis.
copy.tl:
Saan nanggagaling ang enerhiya ng ating pagkain?

Halos lahat ng pagkain ay nagmumula sa mga halaman — at ang enerhiya nito ay unang galing sa liwanag ng araw, nakuha sa pamamagitan ng photosynthesis.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang kusog sa atong pagkaon?

Halos tanang pagkaon naggikan sa mga tanom — ug ang kusog niini orihinal nga gikan sa kahayag sa adlaw, nakuha pinaagi sa photosynthesis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All warm objects, including our bodies, give off heat by radiation even if we cannot see it!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a basic fact about radiation but does not identify any advantageous or disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, or radiation, which is the core action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The hotter the object, the more heat it radiates.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat and radiation but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature, which is the required skill. It only states a relationship between temperature and radiated heat, not the conceptual distinction.

copy.en: All warm objects, including our bodies, give off heat by radiation even if we cannot see it! The hotter the object, the more heat it radiates.
copy.tl: Lahat ng mainit na bagay, pati ang katawan natin, ay naglalabas ng init sa pamamagitan ng radiation kahit hindi natin nakikita! Mas mainit ang bagay, mas maraming radiation.
copy.bis: Tanang init nga butang, lakip ang atong lawas, mogawas og init pinaagi sa radiation bisan dili nato makita! Mas init ang butang, mas daghan ang iyang ipagawas nga radiation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are all the same carbon element but have entirely different properties.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that diamond, graphite, and fullerenes are the same carbon element with different properties, which touches on the concept of an element. However, G8-M-4 requires describing pure substances as having fixed chemical composition (with elements/compounds as examples) and that all atoms of an element have a unique number of protons. The card does not address fixed composition, compounds, or protons, so it only shares the broad subject of elements and does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Diamond is very hard, graphite is soft
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions hardness and softness, which are physical properties of solid materials. However, G3-M-5 expects students to describe physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable in the context of everyday solid materials. The card focuses on carbon allotropes and does not provide the guided description of physical properties of common solid materials required at Grade 3. It is only tangentially related through the words 'hard' and 'soft'.

copy.en: Carbon exists as different allotropes! Diamond is very hard, graphite is soft, and fullerenes exist too. They are all the same carbon element but have entirely different properties.
copy.tl: Ang carbon ay umiiral bilang iba't ibang allotropes! Ang diamond ay napakamatigas, ang graphite ay malambot. Pareho silang carbon element pero may magkaibang properties.
copy.bis: Ang carbon naglungtad isip lain-laing allotropes! Ang diamond hilabihan ka-matigas, ang graphite malambot. Silang tanan mao rang carbon element apan adunay hingpit nga lain-laing properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An alloy is a mixture of two or more metals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an alloy as a mixture of metals but does not describe it as a uniform or non-uniform mixture, nor does it connect to solutions or suspensions as required by the competency. It shares the vocabulary 'mixture' but provides no direct instructional support for classifying mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: like bronze from copper and tin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bronze made from copper and tin, which are metals, but it does not identify properties or uses of metals used by the local community. It only gives a composition example, not the properties or uses required by the competency.

copy.en:
What is an alloy?

An alloy is a mixture of two or more metals, like bronze from copper and tin, to make it stronger!
copy.tl:
Ano ang haluang metal o alloy?

Ang alloy ay pinaghalong dalawa o higit pang metal, gaya ng bronze na gawa sa tanso at lata, para mas tumibay!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang alloy?

Ang alloy usa ka sinagol nga duha o labaw pa ka metal, sama sa bronze nga hinimo sa kobre ug tin, aron mas mulig-on!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Alloys have different properties from the metals that make them up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions alloys, which are homogeneous mixtures, but does not describe them as mixtures, classify them as uniform/non-uniform, or give examples of solutions or suspensions. It only states that alloy properties differ from component metals, which does not directly support the competency of describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: steel is much stronger than pure iron or pure carbon all by themselves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions steel and iron, which are metals, but does not identify properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper. It only compares steel's strength to pure iron and carbon, which is not the focus of the competency.

copy.en: Alloys have different properties from the metals that make them up! For example, steel is much stronger than pure iron or pure carbon all by themselves.
copy.tl: Ang mga alloy ay may ibang katangian kaysa sa mga metal na bumubuo nito! Halimbawa, ang steel ay mas matibay kaysa purong iron o purong carbon na mag-isa.
copy.bis: Ang mga alloy adunay lahi nga katangian kaysa sa mga metal nga naghimo niini! Pananglitan, ang steel mas lig-on kaysa purong iron o purong carbon nga mag-inusara.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's just a mixture!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that an alloy is a mixture, but it does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures or give examples such as solutions and suspensions. It only touches on the general concept of mixtures without supporting the specific competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's just a mixture!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address reversibility of physical changes or irreversibility of chemical changes. It only distinguishes a mixture from a new chemical substance, which is not the same as explaining physical vs chemical change reversibility.

copy.en:
Is an alloy a brand-new chemical substance?

Nope, it's just a mixture! The original metals are still hiding inside the alloy, just mixed together.
copy.tl:
Ang aleasyon ba ay isang bagong sustansyang kemikal?

Hindi, isa lang itong halo! Ang mga orihinal na metal ay nasa loob pa rin ng aleasyon, magkahalo lang.
copy.bis:
Ang aleasyon ba usa ka bag-ong kemikal nga substansiya?

Dili, usa lang kini ka sagol! Ang orihinal nga mga metal anaa gihapon sa sulod sa aleasyon, sagol lang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Recycling aluminum cans saves a HUGE amount of energy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions recycling, which is one disposal method, but it does not demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, nor does it address reusing, oil disposal, or recycling paper/plastic/glass. The focus is on energy savings, not on proper handling/disposal practices.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It takes way less power to melt an old can than to make new aluminum from rock.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses energy savings from recycling but does not identify energy as something that can cause change, nor does it mention light, sound, or heat energy. It only implies that less power is needed, which is not the same as teaching the concept of energy causing change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It takes way less power to melt an old can than to make new aluminum from rock.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions melting an old can, which is a change in solid material, but it does not describe how changes in solid materials make them useful through shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, or cutting. The focus is on energy comparison, not on the usefulness of material changes.

copy.en: Recycling aluminum cans saves a HUGE amount of energy! It takes way less power to melt an old can than to make new aluminum from rock.
copy.tl: Nakakatipid ng NAPAKALAKING enerhiya ang pag-recycle ng lata ng aluminyo! Mas kaunting kuryente ang kailangan para tunawin ang lumang lata kaysa gumawa ng bago mula sa bato.
copy.bis: Makadaginot og DAKO KAAYONG enerhiya ang pag-recycle sa lata nga aluminyo! Mas gamay ra nga kuryente ang kinahanglan aron tunawon ang daang lata kaysa maghimo og bag-o gikan sa bato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dental amalgam is a durable, inexpensive alloy of mercury, silver, tin, and copper used for tooth fillings
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions silver and copper as components of dental amalgam and describes the alloy's durability and use in fillings, but it does not teach the properties or uses of the metals themselves (iron, gold, silver, copper) as required by the competency. copy.en: The ant queen no longer leaves to find food — worker ants bring her food, feed her mouth-to-mouth, and clean her so she stays healthy and can keep laying eggs.
copy.tl: Hindi na umaalis ang reynang langgam para kumain — dinadalhan siya ng pagkain ng mga manggagawa, pinapakain bibig-sa-bibig, at nililinis para manatiling malusog at makapangitlog.
copy.bis: Ang reyna nga langgam dili na mogawas aron mokaon — ang mga trabahante magdala og pagkaon ngadto kaniya, magpakaon baba-sa-baba, ug limpyohan siya aron magpabilin nga himsog ug makapangitlog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Worker ants are female ants that cannot have babies — instead they search for food, guard the nest, and take care of the eggs and larvae.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the jobs of worker ants (foraging, guarding, caring for young) but does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It does not directly support the competency's skill of observing examples and explaining interdependence.

copy.en:
What jobs do worker ants do?

Worker ants are female ants that cannot have babies — instead they search for food, guard the nest, and take care of the eggs and larvae.
copy.tl:
Anong trabaho ang ginagawa ng manggagawang langgam?

Ang manggagawang langgam ay mga babaeng langgam na hindi na maaaring magkaanak — sa halip, naghahanap sila ng pagkain, binabantayan ang pugad, at inaalagaan ang mga itlog at larva.
copy.bis:
Unsay trabaho sa manggagawang langgam?

Ang manggagawang langgam mga babaye nga langgam nga dili na makapanamkon — hinuon, nangita sila og pagkaon, nagbantay sa pugad, ug nag-atiman sa mga itlog ug larva.

assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies an antacid as a base and mentions neutralizing acid, but it does not address identifying solutions, litmus indicator reactions, or classifying home/school substances as acids, bases, and salts. It only shares a related example of a base.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Antacid medicine is a special base!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card names antacid as a base and mentions neutralizing stomach acid, but it does not teach identification of common acids, bases, and salts using indicators. No indicator use, no examples like hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, or saline solution, and no identification procedure is provided.

copy.en: Antacid medicine is a special base! It works hard to neutralize any extra acid in your tummy when it feels upset.
copy.tl: Ang antacid na gamot ay isang espesyal na base! Nagne-neutralisa ito ng sobrang asido sa tiyan kapag masama ang pakiramdam mo.
copy.bis: Ang antacid nga tambal usa ka espesyal nga base! Magneutralisa kini sa sobra nga asido sa tiyan kon dili maayo ang imong gibati.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Antacid medicine for an upset stomach is a base! It cancels excess stomach acid by neutralization to relieve that burning feeling.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions neutralization of acid by a base, which is a chemical reaction, but it does not explain how this reaction relates to or impacts the natural or built environments as required by G10-M-4. The competency focuses on reactions like combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration and their environmental impact; the antacid example is a medical application, not an environmental one.

copy.en: Antacid medicine for an upset stomach is a base! It cancels excess stomach acid by neutralization to relieve that burning feeling.
copy.tl: Ang antacid na gamot sa masakit na tiyan ay isang base! Kinakansela nito ang labis na acid sa tiyan sa pamamagitan ng neutralization para mawala ang hapdi.
copy.bis: Ang antacid nga tambal sa sakit nga tiyan usa ka base! Kanselahon niini ang sobra nga acid sa tiyan pinaagi sa neutralization aron mawala ang kasakit.

copy.en: During Northern Hemisphere summer, the Antarctic Circle at 66.5 degrees south is in complete darkness for 24 hours because the South Pole tilts away from the Sun.
copy.tl: Sa panahon ng summer sa Northern Hemisphere, ang Antarctic Circle sa 66.5 degrees timog ay nasa ganap na kadiliman sa loob ng 24 oras dahil ang South Pole ay nakatagilid palayo sa Araw.
copy.bis: Sa panahon sa summer sa Northern Hemisphere, ang Antarctic Circle sa 66.5 degrees sur anaa sa hingpit nga kangitngit sa 24 ka oras tungod kay ang South Pole mikiling palayo sa Adlaw.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the Antarctic Circle and polar day/night phenomena, which is unrelated to describing types of volcanoes, their activity, eruption type, or location in the crust. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: The Antarctic Circle at 66.5 degrees south is the boundary where the Sun does not set during Southern Hemisphere summer and does not rise during Southern Hemisphere winter.
copy.tl: Ang Antarctic Circle sa 66.5 degrees timog ay ang hangganan kung saan ang Araw ay hindi lumulubog tuwing summer sa Southern Hemisphere at hindi sumisikat tuwing winter sa Southern Hemisphere.
copy.bis: Ang Antarctic Circle sa 66.5 degrees sur mao ang utlanan diin ang Adlaw dili mosalop sa summer sa Southern Hemisphere ug dili mosubang sa winter sa Southern Hemisphere.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It almost never rains or snows there.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions precipitation (rain/snow) and coldness, which are weather-related, but it does not teach students to identify the basic characteristics used to describe weather (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, rain, cloud cover). assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lack of precipitation and ice accumulation, which are connected to the water cycle, but it does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It does not describe evaporation, condensation, precipitation, or how the cycle affects ecosystems. The content is only tangentially related.

copy.en: Antarctica is Earth's coldest place, but it's also a desert! It almost never rains or snows there. Its thick ice just piled up slowly over thousands of years.
copy.tl: Ang Antarctica ang pinakamalamig na lugar sa Earth, pero disyerto rin ito! Bihirang umulan o magniyebe doon. Ang makapal na yelo ay dahan-dahang tinipon sa loob ng libu-libong taon.
copy.bis: Ang Antarctica ang pinakabugnaw nga dapit sa Yuta, apan disyerto usab kini! Talagsa ra moulan o moniyebe didto. Ang baga nga yelo natapok hinay-hinay sulod sa liboan ka tuig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Philippine volcanoes can erupt in any month of the year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that Philippine volcanoes can erupt in any month, but does not discuss patterns of eruptions over the last 100 years, predictability, or family/community discussion. The mention of rainy months and mudflows is about lahar, not eruption patterns.

copy.en: Philippine volcanoes can erupt in any month of the year! But during rainy months, fresh volcano ash is much more likely to turn into dangerous mudflows.
copy.tl: Puwedeng pumutok ang mga bulkan sa Pilipinas kahit anong buwan! Pero sa mga maulan na buwan, ang bagong abo ay mas madaling maging putik.
copy.bis: Pwede moabot ang pagputok sa mga bulkan sa Pilipinas bisan unsang bulan! Apan sa ulan nga mga buwan, ang bag-ong abo mas dali mahimong lapok.

copy.en:
Why are apex predators often endangered?

Because they're already few in number and need lots of food and space, apex predators are quickly hurt when forests are destroyed or people hunt them — that's why protecting them matters.
copy.tl:
Bakit madalas nanganganib ang apex predator?

Dahil kakaunti lang sila at marami silang kailangang pagkain at malawak na tirahan, mabilis silang naapektuhan kapag nasisira ang gubat o naghuhuli ang tao. Kaya mahalaga silang protektahan.
copy.bis:
Ngano kanunay nameligro ang apex predator?

Tungod kay gamay ra sila ug nanginahanglan ug daghang pagkaon ug lapad nga puy-anan, paspas sila maapektuhan kon madaot ang lasang o mangayam ang tawo. Mao nga importante silang panalipdan.

assignedReviews.reason: Energy left at the top of a food chain is not trophic levels as levels of energy in a food pyramid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At each step up the food chain, less energy passes along — apex predators are at the very top
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Energy loss up a food chain is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
Why are there so few apex predators?

At each step up the food chain, less energy passes along — apex predators are at the very top, so only a tiny bit of energy reaches them, so they can't be many.
copy.tl:
Bakit kakaunti lang ang apex predator?

Sa bawat hakbang pataas sa food chain, kumakaunti ang enerhiyang inililipat — nasa pinakatuktok ang apex predator, kaya kakaunti lang ang enerhiyang umaabot sa kanila, kaya hindi sila puwedeng dumami.
copy.bis:
Nganong gamay ra ang apex predator?

Sa matag lakang pataas sa food chain, mokunhod ang enerhiya nga gibalhin — ang apex predator naa sa kinatumyan, mao nga gamay ra nga enerhiya ang moabot kanila, mao nga dili sila modaghan.

copy.bis: Ang aphid adunay duha ka gagmayng tubo duol sa iyang ikog nga gitawag cornicles, nga makatabang sa iyang depensa.
